newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary opposition MPs walk out over judge vote.
newsitem.headline: Hungary opposition MPs walk out over judge vote.

text.p: Hungary's parliamentary opposition walked out on Tuesday when its candidate for the constitutional court was rejected despite what it said was an earlier agreement with the ruling coalition.
"This was supposed to be a gentlemen's agreement," Miklos Csapody, MP of the opposition Hungarian Democratic Forum (MDF) party, told Reuters.
In a secret ballot, some 90 MPs voted against the opposition's candidate, Janos Bruhacs, for judge of the constitutional court, he said.
Andras Hollo, candidate of the ruling coalition of socialists and Free Democrats, was approved.
"This was a top level agreement," Csapody said. "I do not think there is any basis for further talks."
Hungary's ruling coalition has a comfortable 72 percent majority over the five opposition parties.
The constitutional court is two judges short and appointment of a new judge needs a four fifths majority.
Hungary's constitutional court handles all complaints regarding unconstitutional bills, decrees or any other case when breach of constitution could be involved.
It has eleven judges, of which two retired over the last two years.
